title: Essential Git commands
description: The Git commands you use every day.

cards.back:
Creates a new Git repository in the current folder.

```!bash
git init
```

Copies a remote repository locally, with its whole history.

```!bash
git clone https://github.com/user/project.git
```

Shows modified files, those ready to commit and the current branch.

```!bash
git status
```

Adds changes to the staging area for the next commit.

```!bash
git add file.txt
```

Records the staged changes in the history, with a message.

```!bash
git commit -m "Message"
```

Sends local commits to the remote repository.

```!bash
git push origin main
```

Downloads changes from the remote and merges them into the current branch (fetch + merge).

```!bash
git pull
```

Lists branches; with a name it creates a new one.

```!bash
git branch new-feature
```

Switches to another branch; with -b it creates it and switches to it.

```!bash
git checkout -b new-feature
```

Merges the history of another branch into the current one.

```!bash
git merge new-feature
```

Shows the commit history; --oneline makes it compact.

```!bash
git log --oneline
```
